newsitem.title: USA: Holder mulls Universal Hospital board move.
newsitem.headline: Holder mulls Universal Hospital board move.

text.p: Boston investor Peter Kamin and entities he controls said last week they were considering whether to seek replacement of the board of Universal Hospital Services Inc following its adoption of a "poison pill."

In a Nov. 22 letter to company president Thomas Minner, Kamin said if he decides to seek to replace the current board he may also decide to attempt it at a special meeting rather than at the company's 1997 annual meeting.

"Our decision on proposing a slate of nominees will, of course, be made based upon a number of factors, including the direction taken by the current board," Kamin said in the which filing late Tuesday with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Among the factors that will influence his decision, Kamin said, is the board's response to a Nov. 5 purchase offer made by an undisclosed company that Universal Hospital said in a Nov. 11 statement was in "a range exceeding the current market price" for its stock. It closed Tuesday at $9.25 a share.
Kamin also asked the board to reconsider a "poison pill" plan that the board adopted on Nov. 8.

The company has said its "shareholder rights" plan gives shareholders the right to purchase a new series of preferred stock, exercisable if a person or group acquired 15 percent or more of its common stock.
Kamin, whose entities include Peak Investment Limited Partnership, holds 425,600 shares of the company's common stock, or 7.8 percent of the total outstanding.
